term: natural-reason profile and descriptive theological horizon
definition: Audience records agents, membership in a selected practice, being theistic and using moves. DescriptiveTheisticHorizon says users of natural-knowability moves are theists and the practice own standards endorse those moves. This is independent of the existing shared-reason predicate. Uniform sharedness, uniform nonsharedness and mixed positive/negative move witnesses compare that same predicate at a fixed meaning.
note: Analyst reconstruction with attribution deferred; the older mixed horizon statement and all supporting source claims remain unchanged. A person can be outside one religious practice while being a theist; internal endorsement does not logically deny outsider-shared standards. The profile does not model neutrality to every possible worldview, actual apologetic history or independent warrant of standards. Encoding such a stronger neutrality claim would require a domain of worldviews and a precise cross-framework admissibility/calibration relation; it is not inferred from non-Christian use. Named uniform coverage remains an explicit open proposition; a mixed pair of witnesses is the further relevant profile.
